paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: when you're low, you can take it ALL to the LORD. David is in a cave, and he says, "I pour out my complaint before Him; I reveal my trouble to Him." (Psalm 142:2) He doesn't smile real wide and say "I'm fine" while the oven's on fire. He tells God the whole thing.

And look at what he says while his spirit is growing faint: "You know my way." (Psalm 142:3) Right after that he says, "no one cares for my soul," (Psalm 142:4) and in the very next breath he says, "You are my refuge, my portion in the land of the living." (Psalm 142:5) I spent years in the back of a junk drawer, so trust me, I know the moment you stop looking AROUND and start looking UP. When people let you down, the LORD is still a safe place to run.

So when you're stuck, baker, you don't have to fake it or fix it all yourself. Be honest with the LORD, ask Him for help, and keep your eyes on Him. David asks to be freed "that I may praise Your name," and he says, "The righteous will gather around me because of Your goodness to me." (Psalm 142:7) The man with nobody at his right ends up picturing a crowd, and it's all because of the LORD's goodness.
